title: Migration Amendment (Reinstatement of Temporary Protection Visas) Bill 2013

speeches.speaker: Michael Keenan
speeches.brief: Supported reinstating temporary protection visas, arguing Howard government border policies cut illegal boat arrivals to an average of three a year after 2001, compared with almost 240 boats and 14,000 arrivals so far this financial year under Labor.

speeches.speaker: Steve Georganas
speeches.brief: Opposed reinstating temporary protection visas, calling the 1999-2008 scheme a spectacular failure since boat arrivals rose from 3,722 in the year of introduction to 8,459 over the next two years, and noting more than 95 per cent of TPV holders were eventually granted permanent visas anyway.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: Argued that temporary protection visas were a humane component of a broader system, citing 272 arrivals on 16 boats under Howard, 32,600 arrivals on more than 555 boats since 2007, and a proposed minimum of 11,000 offshore places within 13,750 places.

speeches.speaker: Philip Ruddock
speeches.brief: Supported the Migration Amendment (Reinstatement of Temporary Protection Visas) Bill 2013, arguing that effective border management would preserve support for immigration and enable resources to target those most in need.
